title: Tech Note: 4D (Is There) for Flex
author: Tim Kaufman, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.
featured_technology: SQL queries from Flex to 4D Server
Flash Player and 4D Web server integration

historical_commentary.text: This technical note demonstrates how to build Rich Internet Applications (RIAs) using Adobe Flex (Flash-based framework) connected to 4D Server via SQL queries, showcasing a particular web 2.0 era pattern that was contemporary circa 2008. The note covers the 4D Web 2.0 Pack's Flex components (SQLService, SQLResultSet), MXML declarative UI syntax, ActionScript 3 event handling, and data binding—technologies that were cutting-edge for web UI development at the time. Flex was marketed as an alternative to AJAX/JavaScript for building complex interactive web clients, offering strong typing and component-based architecture. However, Flex (Flash-based) has been completely superseded by modern web standards (HTML5, JavaScript/TypeScript, modern frameworks like React, Vue, Angular). 4D's modern web strategy (Qodly, 4D Web Components, REST APIs) has moved entirely away from Flash/Flex toward standards-based web technologies.
related_updates: Adobe discontinued Flash/Flex; Flash Player was end-of-life December 2020. No modern browser support.
4D v17+ introduced Qodly, a modern low-code web builder using standard web technologies (HTML5, JavaScript) and ORDA-based REST APIs, replacing the Flex/Web 2.0 Pack approach entirely
Modern 4D web development uses standard frameworks (Vue, React, Angular) with 4D's REST API or GraphQL endpoints, rather than Flex's proprietary SWC components
SQLService and SQLResultSet classes from 4D Web 2.0 Pack are now obsolete; modern data binding uses REST/JSON APIs
